stage.title: Freeze RenderGraph contract and replace the legacy skeleton

goal: Define the latest-only RenderGraph contract before implementation starts. This stage makes RenderGraph the owner of precise resource declarations and removes the old skeleton from the target architecture instead of adapting it.
entry_gate: The RHI submission chain remains RHIExecutor-owned.
CopyScope is the only structured raw-RHI copy queue source.
Raw RHI persistent tracking is constrained to whole-resource state.

hard_rules.rule: Do not preserve RHIGraphicsCommandList-based RenderGraph APIs as compatibility wrappers.
Do not let bindless descriptors imply hidden resource dependencies.
Do not expose public cross-queue Barrier or QueueTransfer authoring through RenderGraph users.
Do not allow AddSetupPass lambdas to create RHI resources, update bindless arrays, record commands, or submit work.
Do not allocate graph-owned pass parameters, RGResource descriptors, or compiled plan data from caller stack lifetime.
Do not model GPU trace scopes as a raw CommandList-local stack when the logical scope can span multiple compiled CommandLists.
Do not add a separate setup lambda to AddPass. AddPass has one execution lambda only; setup belongs to AddSetupPass and parameters belong to graph.Alloc<T>().
Do not declare GPU scopes inside AddPass execution lambdas when the scope describes graph-level lifetime. Use RG_EVENT_SCOPE(graph, name, ...) outside pass execution.
Do not hide native custom GPU work inside ordinary AddPass execution lambdas. Initial external native work must use an explicit platform-command-list external pass contract with declared access.
Do not rely on hidden backend tracker state when sequencing raw RHI, RenderGraph, and later raw RHI work. Boundary state must be carried by import/export receipts.
Do not expose backend platform command-list handles to ordinary AddPass execution lambdas. AddPass records abstract RHI commands only.
Do not execute platform-command-list external callbacks during RG record. They are emitted as RHI commands and executed during backend translate/platform record.

checkpoints.title: Replace legacy RenderGraph surface in the target design
checkpoints.problem: The current RenderGraph code is a commented legacy skeleton with RHIGraphicsCommandList-era concepts. Building around it would keep stale ownership and fake compatibility alive.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: The target design names the existing RenderGraph implementation as replacement work, not a preserved API.
The new public entrypoint is a frame-local RenderGraph allocator/setup/pass/dispatch surface based on RHICommandList and RHIExecutor.
Old classes are either deleted or rewritten in place when implementation starts.

checkpoints.title: Freeze resource access declaration model
checkpoints.problem: Barrier correctness cannot be inferred from arbitrary RHICommandList commands without rebuilding the same complex backend tracker. RenderGraph needs explicit pass declarations.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: Texture accesses declare handle, mip range, array range, aspect, read/write mode, usage state, and queue intent.
Buffer accesses declare handle, byte range, read/write mode, usage state, and queue intent.
External resources are imported with known initial state and exported with required final state.
Bindless resource usage is explicit through the same access declarations.

checkpoints.title: Freeze pass execution and queue model
checkpoints.problem: RenderGraph must compile queue placement and synchronization. If pass lambdas choose queues implicitly during record, the graph cannot own cross-queue correctness.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: Each pass has one declared execution domain: Graphics, Compute, Copy, or Raytracing.
AddPass accepts graph-owned parameters, pass flags, and exactly one execution lambda with the shape [](RHICommandList& cmd_list, RGContext context) { ... }.
The AddPass lambda records abstract RHI commands only and never receives a platform command-list handle.
Setup work is registered through AddSetupPass and a setup context instead of a second AddPass setup lambda.
Copy passes compile to CopyScope or executor-derived copy submit work; users do not manually author queue transfers.
Queue intent is part of compile input and is frozen before command recording starts.
Execution lambdas receive only graph-owned parameters, resolved context data, and the RHICommandList selected by the compiled plan.

checkpoints.title: Freeze raw RHI simplification contract
checkpoints.problem: RenderGraph cannot reduce backend complexity unless raw RHI stops promising precise subresource and range scheduling semantics outside RenderGraph.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: Raw RHI whole-resource persistent state is the only cross-frame backend state contract.
Raw RHI buffer range and texture subresource data are local barrier details, not persistent scheduling ownership.
Unknown first read is invalid unless the resource is imported with known state.
Frame end publishes canonical final state for exported resources.

checkpoints.title: Lock validation contract
checkpoints.problem: RenderGraph implementation will touch RHI scheduling and resource lifetime. Validation must reuse existing project scripts and avoid ad-hoc test wrappers.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: Focused RHI/RenderGraph tests are planned under TestRHITranslate and run through testscripts/windows/test_rhi_translate.ps1.
Milestone-sized changes run testscripts/windows/test_all.ps1.
No standalone RenderGraph validation script is introduced.

checkpoints.title: Freeze RG allocator and parameter lifetime model
checkpoints.problem: RenderGraph setup, compile, and parallel record need stable graph-owned memory. Caller-owned stack objects or ad-hoc heap allocation would make pass parameters, RGResource objects, and compiled plans unsafe across async phases.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: RenderGraph owns a frame-local CPU allocator for PassNode, RGResource, access declarations, graph.Alloc<T>() parameter objects, compiled plan objects, and resolved resource tables.
Setup-phase allocations are mutable only until Compile starts, then treated as frozen input.
Compile-phase allocations produce immutable artifacts consumed by record tasks without graph mutation locks.
Record tasks receive read-only resolved resource tables and graph-owned parameter data with graph lifetime.
Only external imported RHI resources are caller-owned; the RGResource wrappers and pass parameter storage are graph-owned.

checkpoints.title: Freeze cross-CommandList GPU trace scope model
checkpoints.problem: Current GPU scope APIs are CommandList-local begin/end events. Parallel RenderGraph record can split one logical scope across multiple CommandLists and queues, so stack pairing cannot be inferred from record order.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: RG_EVENT_SCOPE(graph, name, ...) declares graph trace scopes outside AddPass execution lambdas and stores stable scope id, parent id, name, and logical lifetime metadata.
Compile assigns scope begin/end emission points to concrete CommandLists after pass grouping and queue segmentation are known.
A scope that spans multiple CommandLists is represented by explicit scope identity and ordering metadata instead of relying on one native command buffer stack.
Nested scopes that cross unordered queues are either compiled with an ordering boundary or rejected with a clear diagnostic.
Pass-local GPU scopes remain allowed only when begin and end are emitted inside the same compiled CommandList segment.

checkpoints.title: Freeze external pass and interop boundary contract
checkpoints.problem: The renderer may need native custom GPU work outside RHICommandList, raw RHI work before and after a graph, and multiple RenderGraph instances in one frame. Without an explicit contract, those paths would reintroduce hidden resource state and allocator lifetime bugs.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: External native work uses a separate AddExternalPass-style contract and does not receive RHICommandList&.
Initial external pass support is limited to platform-command-list interaction; direct GPU runtime submit/sync is rejected.
External passes declare resource reads/writes, native platform command-list requirements, native resource handle requirements, and queue type before Compile.
RG record emits platform-command-list external work as a typed RHI command; backend translate executes the native callback when the platform command list exists.
Raw RHI -> RenderGraph -> raw RHI sequencing uses explicit import/export receipts with whole-resource state, owner queue, and completion boundary.
Multiple RenderGraph instances share RGFrameContext for receipts and global pool access, but keep CPU graph allocation and transient alias allocation per graph.
Cross-graph transient aliasing is not implicit; workloads that require one alias plan must be compiled as one graph.

stage_exit_gate: The new RenderGraph boundary is explicit enough to implement without preserving the old skeleton.
Resource access declarations cover subresource, buffer range, bindless, queue intent, imports, and exports.
The public API shape is graph.Alloc<T>(), RG_EVENT_SCOPE(...), AddSetupPass(...), AddPass(param, flags, execution_lambda), and Dispatch().
External pass and raw RHI/RenderGraph interop boundaries are explicit before implementation starts.
Raw RHI simplification rules are frozen before backend tracker cleanup starts.
RG allocator lifetime and cross-CommandList GPU trace scope correctness are frozen before async implementation starts.
validation: Planning-only checkpoint; no build script is required now.
When implementation lands, use testscripts/windows/test_rhi_translate.ps1 first and testscripts/windows/test_all.ps1 after milestone-sized changes.
implementation_notes: Implemented a latest-only RenderGraph construction surface with graph.Alloc<T>(), AddSetupPass(), AddPass(), Compile(), and Dispatch().
Implemented graph-owned parameter lifetime tracking, explicit texture/buffer access declarations, import/export metadata, RGFrameContext receipts, and deterministic hazard-edge compilation.

Left barrier lowering, CopyScope handoff emission, RHIExecutor submit plans, platform external pass callbacks, GPU trace scope compilation, external pass interop, and focused RHI validation as unfinished checkpoints.
